description: Composite-only orders and narrative for Uber cases — merged on top of member CCS stacks.

U06.chiefComplaint: Collapsed during a marathon with a hot swollen knee, leg pain, low back pain after a fall, and dark urine.
U06.hpiNarrative:
Robert Hayes is a 40-year-old man who collapsed at mile 22 of a charity marathon on a hot afternoon. Witnesses say he stumbled, looked confused, then veered off the course and fell down a rocky embankment — alone for ~45 minutes before rescue.

On arrival: hot monoarticular knee swelling after impact, diffuse thigh and anterior shin pain worse with weight-bearing, new midline low back pain with paraspinal tenderness (mechanism: axial load + tumble), and cola-colored urine. He reports chronic low-grade lumbar stiffness since a motor-vehicle accident ~30 years ago. He joined the marathon to "get fit" despite untreated exertional dyspnea and ankle swelling he has ignored for months.

Workup threads in one admission:
• Knee (#042): hot joint — arthrocentesis before closing septic vs crystal.
• Acute back (#079): fever/flank pattern vs mechanical fall — UA, cultures, CT if complicated.
• Leg (#069): unilateral erythema vs DVT vs compartment — mark borders, venous duplex, ABI if pulses asymmetric.
• Chronic back (#098): radiculopathy red flags after new trauma — SLR, MRI lumbar if deficit.
• Marathon collapse: heat illness, rhabdomyolysis (CK, aggressive fluids), occult HF (BNP, echo), spine imaging if neuro deficit.
U06.clinicalTip: Uber MSK marathon — four CCS pain domains plus collapse physiology. Synovial fluid, venous duplex, CK/renal panel, spine neuro exam, and cardiac screen belong in the same workup.

additionalInterventions.label: Intravenous access
additionalInterventions.why: Large-bore access for fluids, antibiotics, and analgesia — marathon collapse with rhabdo risk.

additionalInterventions.label: CK, serum
additionalInterventions.why: Extreme exertion + immobilization after fall — rhabdomyolysis drives AKI and hyperkalemia.

additionalInterventions.label: BMP / UA / Ca / Phos
additionalInterventions.why: Myoglobinuria (blood+ dipstick, no RBCs), creatinine rise, electrolyte shifts in rhabdo.

additionalInterventions.label: Aggressive IV fluids
additionalInterventions.why: Crystalloid resuscitation — target urine output to flush myoglobin before pigment nephropathy.

additionalInterventions.label: Duplex ultrasound, lower extremities, venous
additionalInterventions.why: Leg pain + immobilization after fall — rule out DVT before attributing pain to cellulitis alone.

additionalInterventions.label: Ankle-brachial index / Arterial Doppler, lower extremities
additionalInterventions.why: Pulse asymmetry or cool foot — arterial insufficiency vs neurogenic claudication in leg-pain thread.

additionalInterventions.label: Physical Exam: Spine / Neuro
additionalInterventions.why: Fall mechanism + chronic back history — motor/sensory level, rectal tone, straight leg raise.

additionalInterventions.label: BNP, serum
additionalInterventions.why: Undiagnosed HF — exertional dyspnea masked as deconditioning until marathon stress.

additionalInterventions.label: Echocardiogram
additionalInterventions.why: If BNP elevated or pulmonary edema — quantify EF and wall motion after exertional collapse.

additionalInterventions.label: CT chest
additionalInterventions.why: When back pain + fever — alternative source; also PE screen if hypoxic with leg pain post-immobilization.

additionalInterventions.label: ECG
additionalInterventions.why: Tachycardia, electrolytes from rhabdo, occult ischemia in 40yo with untreated HF.

U12.precallTitle: I-80 shoulder — Tom slumps on the brake (~25 h before ED)
U12.chiefComplaint: Tremulous, diaphoretic, tachycardic — reports ants crawling on his skin
U12.practiceHpi:
Pre-hospital (~25 hours before the ED)

Tom Hayes is a 45-year-old long-haul truck driver. On a midnight freight run on I-80 he had been drinking in the cab — drowsy but running hot, sympathetic surge, rig at top highway speed. Something tiny on the road ahead made him stomp the brake; the semi swung hard and stopped on the shoulder. He woke at the scene and refused transport.

Emergency department

His partner brought him in. He is tremulous, diaphoretic, and tachycardic. He keeps brushing at his arms and neck — says ants are crawling on his skin and on the curtains. He has not had a drink since yesterday morning. He downplays how much he usually drinks. No witnessed head trauma today.
U12.hpiNarrative:
PRE-HOSPITAL (~25 hours before ED): Tom Hayes, 45-year-old long-haul truck driver, was running a midnight freight leg on I-80. Whiskey bottles rolled in the sleeper cab; he had been drinking through a layover after losing his driving contract. Around hour 18 of the haul he slumped forward on the wheel, foot slamming the brake pedal — the rig lurched to a complete stop on the highway shoulder. A state trooper found him unresponsive at the cab, key still in ignition, cab reeking of alcohol. EMS cleared him at scene after he woke briefly and refused transport.

NEXT MORNING: Partner found him at home shaking, sweating, and "seeing bugs on the wall." Last confirmed drink was a pint of whiskey about 36 hours before ED arrival. He had a seizure and hospital admission for delirium tremens two years ago when he tried to quit. Drinks roughly a liter of whiskey daily when using. Today: anxious, tremulous, tachycardic, oriented but reporting visual hallucinations of insects on the curtain. Job loss last month preceded this relapse. No head trauma, no fever, no focal weakness. He wants help quitting but fears "the shakes getting worse like last time."

Mechanism: GABA downregulation after chronic ethanol → autonomic hyperactivity 24–72 h after last drink; prior DT lowers seizure threshold.

Treatment threads (Uber U12): CIWA benzos (195), DT/seizure risk (035), sedative overlap (109), safety after relapse (172). Thiamine before glucose; folate/B6/multivitamin; ethanol level; addiction and psych consult; DT monitoring.
U12.clinicalTip: Truck-driver pre-call → day-2 withdrawal. Prior DT history — CIWA-driven benzos, thiamine before glucose, ICU threshold, addiction/psych consult, safety assessment.

additionalInterventions.label: CIWA-Ar scoring
additionalInterventions.why: Composite U12 — symptom-triggered benzodiazepines per CIWA for moderate withdrawal with prior DT.

additionalInterventions.label: Monitor for delirium tremens
additionalInterventions.why: Visual hallucinations and prior DT — track fever, agitation, autonomic surge for progression.

additionalInterventions.label: Consult, addiction medicine / substance abuse
additionalInterventions.why: Detox linkage, relapse prevention, and inpatient rehab after medical stabilization.

additionalInterventions.label: Consult, psychiatry
additionalInterventions.why: Job-loss relapse with despondency — psychiatry for mood, safety, and disposition.

additionalInterventions.label: Safety assessment after intentional relapse
additionalInterventions.why: Document suicide risk, supports, and safety plan after deliberate drinking post job loss.
